question: The median of the following observations 10, 11, 9, 12, 10, 10, 12, 10, 9, 11 is:
solution:
The correct answer is **10**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **median** of a set of observations is the value that separates the upper half from the lower half of the data. 

 
 
• To find the median of a set of observations, the data must be arranged in numerical order.
 
 
 
• In this case, the observations are: 9, 9, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 12.
 
• Since there are an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middle values, which in this case are 10 and 10.
 
• The median is therefore 10.
 
• The median is the value that separates the upper half from the lower half of the data
 
• To find the median, the data must be arranged in numerical order
 
• If the number of observations is odd, the median is the middle value
 
• If the number of observations is even, the median is the average of the two middle values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The median is one of several measures of central tendency, which describe where the data is centered.
 
 
• Other measures of central tendency include the mean (average) and the mode (most common value).
 
 
 
• The median is considered to be a more robust measure of central tendency than the mean, as it is not influenced by outliers or extreme values.
 
• The **choice of measure of central tendency** depends on the specific needs of the study and the type of data being analyzed
 
 
• It is important to understand the strengths and limitations of each measure of central tendency
 
• to choose the most appropriate measure for the data being analyzed.
